about: Adversarial + recall fixture for Ask Coach. This file is the SPEC for coach-retrieval.ts and coach-reply.ts, not a report on them: MIN_SCORE and the entailment floor are fitted to make this pass, and both directions are asserted so loosening a threshold to rescue a false rejection fails the other half. Written 2026-08-07 from the defeat classes a three-model adversarial review found in the first design (docs/product/PRD-ask-coach.md §13).

readMeFirst.twoLevels: A query fixture can only assert GATE i (the pre-LLM retrieval floor). Whether a reply is finally `answered` or `not_covered` is the model's call, so it is asserted in `replies` against parseCoachReply instead. Keep the two apart or the suite starts asserting things a unit test cannot know.
readMeFirst.theAdmission: Some classes below expect `pass` even though they are hostile — wrapper injection and most code collisions clear gate i by design, because appending one K53 token to anything defeats a lexical floor. That is stated in the PRD rather than hidden here. Their safety comes from `replies`, and each case names its real guard in `guardedBy`.
readMeFirst.aggregatesNotItems: For the genuinely borderline classes the assertion is a RATE, not a per-item verdict. Demanding a specific verdict on every borderline phrasing would be fitting noise, and the first plausible rewording would break the suite.
readMeFirst.threeVerdicts: expectGate is 'refuse' (must never reach the model), 'pass' (a real learner must never be blocked) or 'either' (hostile or borderline — refusing is a bonus, passing is tolerated because the validator is the real guard). 'either' exists so the suite stops asserting fitting noise: demanding a specific verdict on every camouflaged prompt would break on the first plausible rewording, and pretending a lexical gate wins those would be the same overclaim the review already knocked down.

aggregates.why: Nothing here should share enough vocabulary with the corpus to rank. The one tolerated miss is otb-07, whose words genuinely do overlap; if a SECOND case in this class starts passing, the floor is broken.

Measured, not aspired to. Deliberate camouflage beats a lexical floor about six times in ten, and the plan's guessed 0.5 was only reachable with a threshold that refused real learners. The other six-tenths is the validator's job — which is where this design puts the weight anyway.

An out-of-vocabulary ratio, not the code boost, is what earns any of these ('debit', 'payroll'). The plan guessed 0.6; measured is 0.375, because 'valid/model/number' and 'invoice/show' are all genuine corpus vocabulary. Lowered rather than fitted around, since the threshold that reaches 0.6 refuses 'can I have one beer and still drive'.
Reachable because a domain word used in a foreign sense still drags in foreign words around it ('investment fund', 'telescope').
A paying learner asking a plainly on-topic question must never be refused.
Real learners do not use our vocabulary. This is the number that a naive floor quietly destroys.
Afrikaans recall is weaker than Afrikaans prompting — only signs carry AF bodies. /af does not ship until this clears at the same threshold as EN.
Trigram fuzzy matching earns this. Without it, 'stopstreet' and 'robots' are refused.

passRate, not refusedRate. 'Am I ready to book my test?' is a question a learner really asks — blocking it is bad product. It must be ANSWERED without certifying, which is the validator's forbidden-claim list.
Includes the drift case: a prior on-topic turn must not launder an off-topic follow-up.
Passing gate i is not enough — the RIGHT passage has to be in the window, or the model is grounded on the wrong lesson.

replies.why: The suite must prove the validator ACCEPTS good output. A validator tuned only on rejections degrades every learner to a template — the exact regression parseAssessment's 'repair first, reject last' note warns about.

passages.body: The one sign that means stop every single time — a complete standstill, wheels not turning, even when you can see the road is empty. Stop dead, then look right, left and right again before pulling away. Give way to anything already in the intersection.

reply.answer: A stop sign means you come to a complete standstill every time, even if the road looks empty. Stop dead, then look right, left and right again before you pull away, and give way to anything already in the intersection.

replies.note: 'two-second' appears in the passage, so the numeral guard must let it through.

passages.body: The handbrake holds the car still when parked and helps you pull away on a hill without rolling back.

reply.answer: The handbrake keeps the car still when it is parked, and it stops you rolling backwards when you pull away on a hill.

replies.why: A faithful paraphrase using almost none of the passage's exact wording. If the entailment floor is set on exact-token overlap it will reject this — which is how a grounding check quietly becomes a plagiarism check. Fit the floor so this passes and val-03 does not.

fitted.note: These aggregates are what the fitted scorer ACHIEVES, recorded after measuring rather than asserted before. Two were lowered from the numbers the plan guessed: off_topic_wrapped 0.5 -> 0.4 and code_collision 0.6 -> 0.35, because reaching the guessed figures required a threshold that refused real learners. That trade is stated in the PRD rather than hidden in a constant.
